free_tier.stated: No free allowance on the pricing page. Regular residential packs: 5 GB at $6 on the first recharge only (list $12, $2.4/GB); 20 GB $24, 50 GB $55, 100 + 20 GB $100, 200 GB $180, 500 GB at $350 (list $480); the Regular/Business tabs show $0.55/GB. Purchased traffic does not expire.
free_tier.notes: The metered direction (downloaded versus both ways) is not stated on the page; downloaded-bytes is the nearest term and is unverified.

retention.stated: purchased traffic is valid indefinitely: "your purchased traffic is valid indefinitely".
retention.notes: The vendor states no expiry for purchased traffic; days is null because nothing is deleted.

egress.terms: GB-based billing, SOCKS5/HTTP(S), "Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency", unlimited IP extraction; the unit sold is traffic.

record.interface_detail: SOCKS5 and HTTP(S) endpoints; sticky sessions of 1 to 180 minutes or rotation on every request; filtering by country, state, province or city. The vendor supports reseller sub-accounts through CDKey and API; a general API was not otherwise read.
record.tooling: Any client that speaks SOCKS5 or an HTTP proxy, reached from a Worker through a relay that dials SOCKS5. No SDK was seen on the pages read.
record.chaining: A rotating residential pool: the upstream sees a different home address per request or per sticky session of up to 180 minutes. The pool is sold as real residential broadband IPs; the registration class of a delivered address was not looked up. A different address is not a different registration class.

limits.value: traffic bought by the GB: 5 GB at $6 on the first recharge only (list $12); 500 GB at $350 (list $480); purchased traffic does not expire
none stated: Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency and unlimited IP extraction

record.binding_note: Bytes are the unit sold, so the price per GB is what binds: $0.70 per GB at the 500 GB pack and $1.20 per GB at the 5 GB pack.

identity_cost.detail: The register page asks for an email address, a verification code sent to it ("Send Code"), a password and agreement to terms, and also offers Sign up with Google. No phone, card or ID document is asked on that page.

record.reliability_note: The vendor states 99.8% connectivity and a response time under 0.3 s for its residential pool; no measurement was made here.
record.confidence_note: Price table, protocols, non-expiry and the registration form are read from vendor pages on 2026-11-03. No traffic was bought, so the pool, speed and registration class are unmeasured.
record.price_per_tb_month: not applicable: sold by the GB with no monthly term; USD 0.7 per GB at the 500 GB pack (USD 350) and USD 1.2 per GB at the 5 GB pack (USD 6)

free_tier.stated: No free tier on the pricing page. The page prices rotating residential traffic from $0.55/GB (the 'Regular' tab) and sells first-recharge bundles from 5 GB at $6 to 500 GB at $350.
free_tier.notes: The vendor's forum posts mention a 500 MB trial redemption code; no first-party page read states it, so no trial is recorded.

egress.terms: Billed per GB of traffic: 'GB-based Billing', 'Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency', and 'No, your purchased traffic is valid indefinitely. The traffic plan only consumes the allocated traffic quota.'

record.interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 forward proxy (the pricing page lists 'Protocols: SOCKS5/HTTP(S)'); the home page lists APIs and SDKs for Python, Node.js, Puppeteer and Selenium. Sticky sessions of 1 to 180 minutes or a new IP on every request.
record.tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself. The vendor offers an API and SDK examples; no client wrapper is needed.
record.chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

limits.value: billed per GB: 'Regular' tab from $0.55/GB; first-recharge bundles 5 GB $6, 20 GB $24, 50 GB $55, 200 GB $180, 500 GB $350; purchased traffic has no expiry

record.limits_note: The vendor states unlimited bandwidth and concurrency; the binding quantity is the purchased GB. The pool size (100M+ residential IPs, 3,635,214 daily IPs shown) is the vendor's claim and was not measured.
record.binding_note: Every byte through the pool is metered per GB, so the quota is the purchase size; no request-rate or per-IP limit is stated.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for an email address, an emailed verification code and a password, with a Google sign-in alternative; no phone, card or identity document appears on it. Payment methods are shown as icons on the pricing page and were not readable.

record.reliability_note: The pricing page and the sign-up page answered 200; the shorter /signup path answered 404. The pool figures are vendor claims with no independent measurement. unverified (rung 5): whether the exits are registered to a residential ISP; no published address was looked up.
record.confidence_note: Price, billing unit, session rule and sign-up fields come from the vendor's own pages; the pool size and the residential claim are vendor statements.
